newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close higher despite profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close higher despite profit taking.

text.p: Light profit taking pared best levels in CME live cattle futures late but the market closed firmer on the strong tone to cash cattle, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.650 to 0.150 cent per lb higher with April up most at 66.350 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.175 to 0.650 cent a lb higher with March up least at 68.175 cents.

Some of the recent buyers in live cattle took light profits late which trimmed gains. Futures advanced early on active feedlot trade late Wednesday and stronger-than-week-ago cash prices. Feedlots appear to be very current in their marketings after this week's active sales, traders said.
"The $64 trade late yesterday was the main thing holding up the front end," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.
But Skold noted that trading ahead of Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report limited gains in deferreds in light of the wide range of estimates on placements.
"I think that they (USDA) undercounted December and some of those placements could show up in the January number, that's probably keeping the summer contracts down" he said.
But other analysts look for only moderate placements compared with light placements, last year.

The average of analysts' estimate on the report for cattle on feed at feedlots of 1,000 head or more in the seven key states on February 1 was 103.9 percent of a year ago in a range of 101.5 to 105.4 percent. January placements averaged 107.5 percent and ranged from 99 to 114.6 percent and January marketings averaged 101.3 percent of a year ago and ranged from 99 to 104 percent of last year.
R.J. O'Brien sold some April contracts back late after buying early. Cargill Investor Services bought early and Refco bought midday lifting April to its high, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures contnued to follow the lead of live cattle futures in light dealings. Lower corn futures added to support, traders said.

Smith Barney bought March early while R.J. O'Brien and Rosenthal Collins sold, traders said. RBH continued to buy May and Refco bought late after selling early. Cargill spread long December live cattle/short August feeders and Dean Witter sold April and bought deferred feeders, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.02 at $69.19 per cwt.
Futures will trade in normal hours on Friday but will be closed on Monday in observance of Presidents Day.
